$comment: SHRINK-ONLY and hand-edited under review: the checker reports a stale entry (it passes
since #26586), so a site that gets fixed is named for deletion on every run; a stale row
re-licenses its key until it is deleted. An entry whose file is still on disk but was not
read by the scan is refused, so a dead scan stays red. There is deliberately
no `--fix`/`--update` flag — a generator would let a new violation be admitted by
'just run the update command', which is precisely how a gate stops meaning anything.
Every entry must name WHY it is still here and WHAT closes it.
Empty on purpose: the three instances this gate was written from (#4769, #4771, #4772)
were all fixed before it landed, and the gate is clean on the `main` it landed on.
The bidirectional proof is in the PR — it reports the #4771 and #4772 shapes on their
pre-fix commits. A gate that has only ever been green cannot be told apart from a gate
Key format: rule A `<file>::<unit>.<phase>()::<service>`; rule B `<file>::<function>::<registries>`.
Run the checker to see the exact key it computes for a finding.
